readerValues.programmeDescription: Natural and Social Sciences (Bèta-gamma) combines natural and social sciences at the University of Amsterdam. Students study a common first year, then specialise in a major while continuing interdisciplinary project work.
readerValues.comparisonExplanation: This qualified comparison assesses 69 EC of Bèta-gamma’s common natural- and social-science curriculum, including Projects 1–3 with the illustrated mathematics and consultancy choices. The UCR programmes offer different combinations of Earth and society, responsible computing, or cognition and institutions. They do not reproduce all natural-science, urban, philosophy-of-science or interdisciplinary-project formation. Later major study, Project 4, final research and complete progression are excluded.

curriculum.limitation: All 174 documented EC remain visible. Only the 69 EC common curriculum is assessed. The other 105 listed EC (69 EC in the published major and 36 EC of genuine elective space) and the remaining 6 EC Project 4 are excluded. The Academic Skills requirement for Project 4 remains unresolved. Later major courses follow the plan applicable when the major begins; this is not a certified complete 180 EC pathway.

componentNotes.uva-58848: One of two mathematics variants. This illustration retains the Mathematics B variant for natural-science preparation.
componentNotes.uva-58713: Introduces social-scientific perspectives on states, power and society.
componentNotes.uva-57158: Develops programming in Python and examines AI and society. Academic-skills assignments are integrated into the current course.
componentNotes.uva-60890: Studies the origins and development of the universe and life. The current course carries 9 EC.
componentNotes.uva-57369: Introduces cognition across disciplinary perspectives. The current 6 EC course includes academic-skills work.
componentNotes.uva-58648: Introduces research methods and the analysis of scientific research. Students must have followed it before Project 1.
componentNotes.uva-61112: Studies urban life through disciplinary and interdisciplinary perspectives.
componentNotes.uva-58767: Studies emergence across scientific domains. Mathematics, natural-science and programming foundations provide preparation.
componentNotes.uva-60749: Students develop and conduct multidisciplinary research and present it at a symposium. Entry requires having followed the first-year research-methods course.
componentNotes.uva-61107: Analyses interdisciplinary research and prepares for Project 4. Entry requires passing Project 1.
componentNotes.uva-58560: One of two practice-project choices. Students develop sustainability advice for an external organisation; the other choice is Placemaking.
componentNotes.uva-58666: A compulsory Earth Sciences course on plant–soil interactions. Major entry requires at least 48 EC from the Bèta-gamma first year. This component is outside the assessed 69 EC common curriculum.
componentNotes.uva-59720: A compulsory practical course, including fieldwork and reporting. Passing its fieldwork and field-report components prepares for Desertification. This component is outside the assessed 69 EC common curriculum.
componentNotes.uva-59732: A required 3 EC introduction to programming in R. This component is outside the assessed 69 EC common curriculum.
componentNotes.uva-58607: A required 3 EC remote-sensing course. Its attendance requirement must be met before Digital Earth. This component is outside the assessed 69 EC common curriculum.
componentNotes.uva-58645: A required Earth Sciences course on food systems and ecosystems. This component is outside the assessed 69 EC common curriculum.
componentNotes.uva-59727: A required course on water-related Earth-system challenges. This component is outside the assessed 69 EC common curriculum.
componentNotes.uva-58797: A required 3 EC course. Entry requires meeting the Remote Sensing attendance requirement; its own attendance requirement must be met before Desertification. This component is outside the assessed 69 EC common curriculum.
componentNotes.uva-58921: A required 3 EC course on developing evidence from data. This component is outside the assessed 69 EC common curriculum.
componentNotes.uva-58813: Includes fieldwork. Entry requires passing the Plant-Soil Practical fieldwork and field-report components, or the specified earlier equivalent, and meeting the Digital Earth attendance requirement. This component is outside the assessed 69 EC common curriculum.
componentNotes.uva-59729: A compulsory Earth Sciences course in water management. This component is outside the assessed 69 EC common curriculum.
componentNotes.uva-58949: A 6 EC research-design course alongside the bachelor project. The formal rules apply the Future Planet Studies entry conditions to Bèta-gamma major students: completion of the first year and at least 42 EC from year two. This component is outside the assessed 69 EC common curriculum.
componentNotes.uva-58527: An 18 EC supervised individual research project and thesis. Bèta-gamma students follow the Future Planet Studies entry conditions and must choose an Earth-science topic. The general requirement is completion of the first year and at least 42 EC from year two. This component is outside the assessed 69 EC common curriculum.
componentNotes.uva-open-electives: The Earth Sciences plan leaves 36 EC for genuine electives. At most 12 EC may be at any bachelor level; the remaining space uses second- or third-year courses. A completed official Dutch minor can replace these level conditions. Courses must avoid excessive overlap; other arrangements require written examination-board approval. This component is outside the assessed 69 EC common curriculum.
